title: DR1's addresses hub shows each party's full selected address under its own heading; the frontend hub shows the party's name and nothing else.

finding.frontend: The hub is a single govukSummaryList (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/template.njk:11). Each party is one row: the key holds the party title and its hint, the value holds the selected record's name or "Not added yet", and the action is one Add/Change link (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:32-46). The row is built from `parties[party.id]?.name` (:49), so once a party is answered the only thing on the page is an organisation name — no address lines, no country. A trader with two similarly-named records in their address book cannot tell from the hub which one is on the notification, and the hub is the page they are sent back to after every address spoke.
finding.prototype: Each party is a `<section>` with its own h2 heading and a hint paragraph (app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:48-50). When an address is held the section carries a govuk-inset-text block holding the record name on its own line, then every address line, then a Change link (:60-68). dr1-roles-and-addresses-complete shows this for all six sections at once — "Green Valley Farm" over five Romanian address lines under Place of origin, "Northern Livestock Imports Ltd" over three lines under Consignee and Importer, and the CPH number rendered in the same inset shape (:77-83).
finding.difference: Replace the summary list with one section per party: h2 heading, hint paragraph, and — when the party is answered — an inset block carrying the name, every address line and the country, with a Change link beneath it. Give the CPH row the same treatment, which is what DR1 does with it. Nothing new has to be fetched: resolveParties already returns the full record for every answered party on this request (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:60-62), and the picker already renders address lines from the same shape (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/view-model/address-lines.js).
finding.falsifiedBy: An answered frontend hub rendering any address line beneath the party name.
finding.correction: Verified, no change, with one caveat about what was watched rather than read. The DR1 side is fully observable: the answered hub renders six inset blocks, one per section, and the place-of-origin one holds "Green Valley Farm" over five Romanian lines with a Change link inside the inset, exactly as claimed, while the CPH section takes the same shape around "12/345/6789". The frontend hub in the corpus is captured unanswered — every row reads "Not added yet" — so the claim that an answered row shows a bare organisation name comes from the row builder, which puts `parties[party.id]?.name` in the value cell and offers no second line. That is unambiguous in the source, and the structural half of the claim, one summary-list row per party with the title and hint in the key, is visible in the capture. Counting the DR1 rows did not mislead: on the answered hub the Change link sits in the same `__section-action` paragraph an unanswered section's Add link uses, distinguished only by an extra class and by being nested inside the inset, and it was the six insets that were counted, not the six links. CONTROL DROPPED, AND NOTHING IS LOST BY IT. This finding also named 'Not added yet'. That is the same placeholder on all six rows of fe-addresses-hub, so the resolver refused to pick one of them — rightly, because nothing about the string says which row was meant — and it resolves to nothing at all on the DR1 side, where an unanswered section carries an Add link and no placeholder text. It is not a control anyone could point at, and it needs no crop of its own: the Place of origin crop already frames the whole row, key, hint, the words 'Not added yet' and the Add link together, which is the row this finding argues about. 'Place of origin' is now the finding's only control, and it resolves on all three named screens.

relatedTo.why: the copy shortcuts live in the same per-section block, in the branch that runs when no address is held
